Ticket T-0007: Pin the documented error codes of the LLM provider directory and model discovery.
You are the Llm Steward (seat `harness-core-llm-steward`) of the `harness-core` division, working this ticket in your own git worktree on your own branch.
Task: Problem: the configurable-provider directory and model discovery document stable error codes in packages/llm/llm/README.md:15-17 (`INVALID_DIRECTORY`/`DUPLICATE_DIRECTORY` for `registerConfigurableProviders`, `INVALID_DISCOVERY`/`DUPLICATE_DISCOVERY` for `registerModelDiscovery`) and the source documents `REGISTRATION_DISPOSED` for a disposed handle (packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:266 and :289). The throws live at packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:377, :461, :464, :468, :480, :494, :525, :528 and :558, but every test reaching them matches message text only (packages/llm/llm/tests/topology.spec.ts:159-232), and no file under any tests directory in the repository contains `INVALID_DIRECTORY`, `DUPLICATE_DIRECTORY`, `DUPLICATE_DISCOVERY` or `REGISTRATION_DISPOSED`. A code rename would pass every gate while breaking configuration surfaces that branch on the code.

Required: add packages/llm/llm/tests/directory-error-codes.spec.ts that drives each path through the public `ctx.llm` service (build the context the way topology.spec.ts does) and asserts an `LlmError` with the exact `code`: an empty entry list and an entry with an empty `settingsPath` segment give `INVALID_DIRECTORY`; a provider declared twice in one call, a provider another registration already declares, and `handle.replace()` naming a provider another registration owns give `DUPLICATE_DIRECTORY`; `replace()` on a disposed directory handle and on a disposed adapter registration give `REGISTRATION_DISPOSED`; an empty namespace and a discovery without a provider give `INVALID_DISCOVERY`; a second discovery offer for one namespace gives `DUPLICATE_DISCOVERY`. Assert codes, not messages, and assert that the rejected call left the previous state intact where the README promises all-or-nothing.

Ticket T-0023: Stop the translation-prompt snapshot from embedding the gold-pair documents.
You are the Translation Pairing Policy Standard Author (seat `governance-translation-pairing-standard-author`) of the `governance` division, working this ticket in your own git worktree on your own branch.
Task: Problem: scripts/verify-translation-prompt.ts:27-40 reads five live gold pairs (README.md, docs/development.md, docs/i18n/README.md, docs/i18n/translation-rules.md, and .agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-02-bilingual-docs-and-pairing-gate.md with their .zh.md sides) as the reviewed examples, and scripts/verify-translation-prompt.ts:89 prints the whole assembled request in `--snapshot` mode. scripts/snapshots/translation-prompt-v4/request-response.expected.json therefore embeds every byte of those ten documents: its example messages are 4852, 3729, 18191, 10323, 13129, 6387, 9364, 4327, 9713 and 4488 characters of gold-pair text, and the file is 145,899 bytes. scripts/translation-prompt.snapshot.ts:30 compares that file byte for byte, so an edit to any of the ten documents fails the snapshot although nothing about the prompt changed. The expected file was re-recorded for exactly that reason in a8b4eff3e and 21f6aa1f5 (both 2026-09-27), 58558b5ba (2026-09-19), cd40049b4 (2026-09-06), a20497072 and d3f69e20a (2026-08-12 and 2026-08-13); `git log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short -- scripts/snapshots/translation-prompt-v4/` lists them.

Required: make the recorded snapshot independent of the example documents' bodies while it still proves what it proves today: that the request assembles as system, five example pairs, then the source document (scripts/verify-translation-prompt.ts:69-72), that the rendered system prompt is stable, and that the recorded response is consumed correctly. In `--snapshot` mode, print each example message as `{ "role": "user" | "assistant", "example": "<repository path of that side>" }` in place of its `content` (a byte count or hash would change with the documents and defeat the purpose), keep the system message and the source-document message verbatim, and keep the `response` object unchanged; the non-snapshot verify mode keeps reading and checking the live pairs.
